cause.text: The portal module state/tradingCalendar.ts is a generated copy of the frontier's answer, made when the frontier's hard-coded fallback set (NYSE_HOLIDAYS_FALLBACK) spanned 2024-2027, so the module covered 2024-2027 only. The frontier's fallback set was since widened to 2010-2027 (lib/trading_calendar.py blob f54f5589c4, calendar_source NYSE/hardcoded-fallback-2010-2027 under the python that ran) and the portal module was never regenerated. F40-AC5 re-derives every covered day AND asserts the frontier's first fallback year equals the module's firstYear; the days it compared all agreed (1461 of 1461) but expect(frontier.fallback_years[0]).toBe(TRADING_CALENDAR.firstYear) received 2010 against 2024. The module named its source blob 1bb4e9b9fd, the frontier was at f54f5589c4: stale generated artifact, not a hand-edited copy and not a frontier fault.

one_frontier.text: lib/trading_calendar.py, its NYSE_HOLIDAYS_FALLBACK set (2010-2027) read through trading_days_between and calendar_source. The portal's state/tradingCalendar.ts is generated from it by the repository's existing generator; the covered years are the span of the frontier's fallback set, so the portal's years follow the frontier and are never typed in the portal.

regenerate_command: cd <workspace>/portal && node src/pages/InvestorReporting/__tests__/fe-s-40/gen-trading-calendar.mjs   (PYTHON env names the interpreter if python on PATH is not the one; the frontier file must be committed and unmodified)

data_changed.years_2024_to_2027: unchanged: the 41 closed weekdays are identical before and after
data_changed.served_effect: a window boundary dated 2010-2023 was previously compared as written with a limitation note; it is now normalised to trading days (closed-day-only differences read as the same window). Dates 2024-2027 label as before; dates before 2010 or after 2027 are still not claimed (null).

test_change: window.test.ts F40-AC4 recorded test: the out-of-range start year was a typed 2019, now covered; it is read from the module as firstYear - 1 (2009). Assertions unchanged.
